To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the DID using equidistant periods and FEs estimations are less biased and more efficient than other regression‐ based estimations in estimating the TT; and (2) the relative performance of different regression‐based estimates is sensitive to the relative magnitudes and sources of pure selection biases.

DID using equidistant windows and FEs estimations have smaller bias and standard errors than other regression‐ based estimators when there are three sources of pureselection bias: (a) heterogeneous response bias, (b) time‐invariant unobservables (FEs), and (c) intertemporal dependence.

(1) the relative importance of each of three sources of selection bias varies in different contexts and (2) the DID using equidistant time periods and FEs estimations are less biased and more efficient than other regression estimators.

understanding which regression‐based estimator works best and under what conditions.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DID using equidistant periods and FE estimators perform better than other regression‐ based estimators in terms of bias and efficiency in the presence of pure selection bias.
DID and FEs estimations are less biased and more efficient than other regression‐ based estimators in the presence of multiple sources of selection bias.

FEs estimators perform better than the DID estimator, and the FEs estimator is the best of the regression‐based estimator in estimating the TT when there is a large amount of time‐invariant heterogeneity and/or intertemporal dependence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FEs estimators perform best in estimating the TT in the presence of heterogeneous response bias and time‐invariant heterogeneity.
the DID estimator using equidistant periods and the FEs estimator perform well in terms of minimizing selection bias on unobservables, especially in the presence of time‐invariant heterogeneity.
the best‐performing regression‐based estimator is DID using equidistant periods.

the choice of the estimator is critical for estimating the TT and that it is important to account for the relative magnitudes and the nature of selection bias.
